## Summary

Lite-On was started in 1975 by former Texas Instruments employees in
Taiwan, is headquartered in Taipei, and in 1983 became the first
technology company listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange; it makes LEDs,
semiconductors, chassis, monitors, motherboards and optical drives, branched into computer
power supplies, and sold its SSD business to Kioxia in 2020 [1]. The
IEEE registry lists 66 MA-L blocks and one MA-S block to "Liteon
Technology Corporation", mostly at 90 Chien 1 Road, Zhonghe, New Taipei
City, with single blocks under the spellings "LITE-ON Technology Corp."
and "Lite-On Technogy Corp." at the Neihu head office and "LiteON" at
the Chien 1 Road address [2][4].

A MAC in a Lite-On block is most likely a Lite-On wireless module inside
another brand's notebook or device, so the OUI names the module maker,
not the product [3]. DeviWiki lists most Lite-On products with FCC IDs
under grantee code PPQ, among them WCBN combo modules with 802.11abgn plus ac
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 3.0 to 4.2 LE, built on Qualcomm Atheros (QCA9379,
QCA9377, QCA6174A), MediaTek, Marvell (88W8997P, 88W8897), Broadcom
(BCM43569, BCM4352) and Realtek (RTL8812AU) chipsets, and records no
802.11ax module [3]. Whether the address is randomised is up to the
host operating system, so randomization is unknown here. No security
advisory was consulted, so security_notes is empty rather than clean.
